name: The Field household at 1905 Prairie Avenue
head: pa1904_field_marshall

present_on_scene_date.note: Listed at 1905 Prairie Avenue in the Blue Book for 1904 (canvass begun September 1903) and again in the 1905 edition (canvass begun September 1904), which bracket 1 July 1904. The 1905 list prints: 1905 Marshall Field.

associated_with.note: The Blue Book's Prairie Avenue street list prints the household at 1905, and the 1905 list again. The book gives no date the household came or went, so neither end is dated here.

not_in_this_household.note: WHO IS NOT ON THIS CARD, AND WHY. The Blue Book is a society register: it names the family members who received and were received, prints unmarried daughters only as '& dr.', and names no young children, servants, coachmen, cooks or nurses. The 1900 census (ED 40, T623 roll 245) was read for this card. The five live-in staff it lists at the house on 1 June 1900 are on the card, graded inferred because the count was taken four years before the scene. A coachman's wife and children in the rear building are named in his note rather than carded. The 1910 census was not read. A person goes on this card when a source names them, and not before.

persons.name: Marshall Field
persons.note: The 1900 census lists Marshall Field here as head, born August 1834, in Massachusetts, widowed, dry goods merchant (ED 40, sheet 4A, line 34, leaf n800).

persons.note: Enumerated on 1 June 1900 in the house, as a servant (cook); born September 1858 (the figures are hard to read), in Sweden, came to the United States in 1889, single. Servants changed places often, so this records who worked here in 1900; no source read says whether this person was still here on 1 July 1904.
